figures.caption: Figure 3: Ablation overlay on Qwen3-8B: TaPR vs. GRPO trajectories on LCB-219 across training steps. TaPR reaches its pooled pass@3 peak by step 300; GRPO remains near baseline early and closes most of the pooled gap at step 300. Table 3 reports the corresponding Hard-subset comparison.

Figure 2: Qwen3-8B pass@1 and pass@3 on LCB-219 across checkpoints. Dashed lines denote the untrained checkpoint and shading marks the selected step 300. The pass@3 curve peaks at step 300 and returns to baseline at step 500; pass@1 is identical at steps 0, 300, and 500.

Table 1: Public results grouped by backbone. Within each model–benchmark-family block, ∆pp is measured from the lowest displayed untrained checkpoint. Cross-protocol differences are descriptive because benchmarks and inference protocols differ. TaPR uses LCB-219 (n = 219 per model), except for APPS-300.

Figure 1: Overview of Test-aware Policy Refinement (TaPR). The upper path illustrates multi-turn code generation where execution feedback is converted into a dense per-turn test-pass reward; the lower path contrasts standard GRPO, which provides only sparse final-answer feedback.
